summary: Lisboa is a dense, puzzly Vital Lacerda eurogame about rebuilding earthquake-ravaged Lisbon, layering multi-use cards, market speculation, and tile-placement into an intricate engine. It's a heavy, brain-burning experience that rewards careful long-term planning and combo-building over direct conflict.
praised: strong theme integration for a heavy euro
criticised: steep learning curve and rules overhead
iconography and setup can be intimidating

interaction.kind: market manipulation and competitive tile/area claiming

scoring.why: points come from building types, church influence, factory production, and end-game majorities all combined
